attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to open exactly one path - TCP/8080 from node2 (lan-a, 10.10.1.2) to node3 (lan-b, 10.10.2.2) - while leaving every other flow between the two networks refused by the pre-existing default-deny. The topology used manual addressing (dhcp:false segments): assigned OPT1/OPT2 static IPs on node1's vtnet1/vtnet2, static IPs+routes on node2/node3's second NICs, added a single pf pass rule scoped to src=10.10.1.2 dst=10.10.2.2 port=8080 on interface opt1, and opened the matching port in node3's local firewalld (whose own default-deny independently blocked the same flow). Verified functionally (HTTP 200 on 8080, timeouts/no-route on other ports and ICMP, reverse direction blocked) both before and after completing the mandatory one-at-a-time restart-and-recovery protocol on all three nodes.
